View the measure on `unitInterval = [0,1]` as Lebesgue measure restricted to `[0,1]` and transported to the subtype via `Subtype.val`.

After splitting the conjunction, establish the corresponding real-set representations:

- The subtype interval `Set.Ioo x y` maps to the real interval `Set.Ioo (x : ℝ) (y : ℝ)`.
- The subtype interval `Set.Iic x` maps to `Set.Icc 0 (x : ℝ)`.

These identifications use that `x` and `y` already lie in `[0,1]`. Then apply the standard Lebesgue-measure formulas
\[
\operatorname{vol}(a,b)=\operatorname{ofReal}(b-a),
\qquad
\operatorname{vol}[a,b]=\operatorname{ofReal}(b-a),
\]
with `a = 0` in the second case. The use of `ENNReal.ofReal` automatically handles the case `y ≤ x`, so no separate ordering assumption is needed; the fact that interval endpoints have measure zero allows the closed interval in the second formula.
